lead: The Reserve Bank kept the repo rate at 7.25% in a narrow 4-3 vote as inflation climbed to 5.2%, while the health department scrambles to ease medicine shortages worsened by 30 shipments held up at Durban's port.

items.title: Motsoaledi tells doctors to switch to substitute drugs as shortages spread
items.summary: The health minister says circulars will list acceptable alternatives, provinces may buy from other suppliers, and ARV stock for about 6.1 million patients is sufficient, with gaps blamed on logistics and unpaid bills in three provinces.

items.title: 30 medicine shipments stuck at Durban container terminal
items.summary: Motsoaledi asked Transport Minister Barbara Creecy to speed their release. Officials told Parliament the list of at-risk medicines has grown to 184, and Transnet says it will prioritise urgent pharmaceutical cargo at Durban.

items.title: eThekwini's new council meets on Tuesday as coalition talks intensify
items.summary: The 223-seat council sits on 24 November at the Durban Exhibition Centre to elect a mayor and speaker. MK holds 86 seats, short of a majority; the ANC in KZN confirms it is talking to MK.

items.title: MK, ANC, ActionSA and EFF set up teams to negotiate metro governments
items.summary: A proposal on the table would hand MK Durban's mayoralty, ActionSA Johannesburg and Tshwane, and the ANC Ekurhuleni, but no deal is final and the DA says it still wants to lead eThekwini.

items.title: Severe storm warning for most of KZN today
items.summary: The weather service issued a yellow level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms with localised flooding and small hail over most of KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng and parts of the Free State, North West and Mpumalanga.

items.title: Soweto storm leaves one dead and a schoolgirl missing
items.summary: Tuesday's rain and hail flooded homes in Dobsonville and Zola. A man's body was recovered and searchers are combing a 4km area for an 11-year-old girl believed swept into a stream.

items.title: World Court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice found against Myanmar in the case brought by The Gambia, the first time the court has held a state responsible for genocide.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin issue joint 'peace declaration' in China
items.summary: After a 90-minute meeting on the APEC sidelines, the leaders pledged UN reform and more refined fuel supplies, according to Chinese state media and the Kremlin. Washington had not yet commented.

items.title: Houthi missile attack damages tower in Riyadh as Gulf conflict widens
items.summary: A building in Riyadh's financial district was hit in an apparent Houthi strike, while Iran targeted sites in Kuwait and Bahrain. Trump says he will 'see what happens' after 1 January.

items.title: Crimean Bridge hit for the third time this week, Russia says
items.summary: Moscow blamed Ukraine and suspended rail traffic, while the European Commission proposed a $49.5bn loan to Kyiv for 2027, repayable only after Russia pays reparations.

items.title: DRC-Rwanda peace deal stalls over security commitments
items.summary: A year after the Washington Accords, the two sides still disagree on neutralising the FDLR militia and Rwanda lifting its defensive measures; a new round of talks was reportedly due in Geneva.

items.title: South Korea's top court overturns ex-PM Han's martial-law conviction
items.summary: The Supreme Court ordered a retrial for former prime minister Han Duck-soo over the December 2024 martial law decree.

items.title: Reserve Bank holds repo rate at 7.25%, warns it may hike again
items.summary: The MPC split 4-3, with three members wanting a 25bp rise. Inflation is now seen returning to the 3% target only in Q3 2028, and 2026 growth stays forecast at 1.2%. Prime remains 10.75%.

items.title: October inflation jumps to 5.2% on fuel costs
items.summary: Consumer inflation rose from 4.5% in September, with core at 4.2%. The MPC noted petrol is close to R30 a litre, compared with about R21 a year ago.

items.title: Rand slides to a year low near R17.35 as dollar strengthens
items.summary: The rand weakened past R17.34 against a dollar near a 19-month high, and the JSE All Share fell 3.7% with resources stocks down 6%.

items.title: Big petrol cut on the cards for December
items.summary: Mid-month Central Energy Fund data point to petrol dropping about R2.65 (93) to R2.90 (95) a litre, with diesel mixed. Official prices are due around 2 December.

items.title: Rassie Erasmus banned for six Tests ahead of Boks v Ireland
items.summary: World Rugby suspended the Springbok coach from match-day duties over comments on officiating after the France Test. SA Rugby wants a full hearing; the Boks face Ireland in Dublin on Saturday.

items.title: Bafana top AFCON qualifying group after win in Nairobi
items.summary: Relebohile Mofokeng scored twice as South Africa beat Kenya to move above Guinea in Group D. Qualifying ends in March against Guinea away and Eritrea at home.

items.title: Sundowns lead Pirates by a point; AmaZulu third
items.summary: Sundowns have 26 points, Pirates 25 and AmaZulu 22. League action resumes on Tuesday with Durban City hosting Polokwane City; AmaZulu host Milford on 28 November.

items.title: Proteas head to Centurion for second Bangladesh Test
items.summary: The second Test of the two-match home series runs from 23 to 27 November at SuperSport Park.

items.title: Anthropic prices record IPO at $83 a share
items.summary: The AI company priced its listing above the expected range and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, in what is reported as the largest US IPO on record.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon model
items.summary: The new mid-tier model offers a one-million-token context window at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, via the API and Gemini subscriptions.

items.title: Data centres to add 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA warns
items.summary: The energy agency says the US and China are leaning on fossil fuels to power AI growth.
